desktop host chain and first product

for_status.evidence: ADR-058 explicitly defines the 7341 bridge as read-only over Core and forbids Orchestrator instantiation.
ADR-071 is an accepted dedicated-apps decision whose read-only bridge boundary is only partially superseded by ADR-080.
The sealed code declares POST mission approval and rejection. Approval invokes `atlas update approve` then may invoke `atlas update apply`; rejection invokes `atlas update reject`.
HTTP middleware records `request.state.auth_identity`, but these mission handler signatures do not accept or pass it to the CLI.

The dossier reopens the prior closure because the two mission routes lie outside ADR-080's Product OS exception and records missing identity propagation, idempotency, HTTP receipt, and ambiguous-result recovery tests.

against_or_limiting_evidence.evidence: ADR-080 is an explicit operator decision, not merely chronology. It partially supersedes the blanket read-only claim for the Fase 15 product_routes mutation surface and adds Merkle receipt coverage for Business Core activate/reject.
Product receipt tests exist for Business Core activate/reject, so that limited path is not evidence that every mutating route lacks audit evidence.
The mission routes use a subprocess rather than instantiate Orchestrator in the bridge; this preserves one ADR-058 constraint but does not authorize the mutation boundary.

explicit_relations.runtime_evidence: Historical 2026-08-12 listener/OPTIONS evidence only; no mutating POST was run in this audit.
explicit_relations.falsifier: If all 13 historical/currently mutating routes are shown inactive behind flags or demo-only, restoring strict read-only becomes materially cheaper.
